title: Load, clean, and plot a messy lettings export
brief: Load a messy CSV of rental listings, clean it with pandas, summarise it with groupby and pivot tables, plot it with matplotlib, and show that cleaning cuts the honest test error of a straight-line fit.
hints: A comparison on a column with missing values gives <NA>. Fill the mask with False (Series.fillna(False)) before you combine masks with & or |, or rows with a missing period end up converted as monthly.
parse_number needs the first run of digits only: in "58 m2" the 2 belongs to the unit. Series.str.extract with a regex like r"(\d[\d,]*\.?\d*)" takes just the leading number.
parse_dates: try one format at a time with pd.to_datetime(text, format=..., errors="coerce") and fill the gaps with Series.fillna. Day comes first in "04/03/2023".
clean_listings: drop duplicates before you compute the quartiles, and compute the fence on rent per m2 (not on rent) after the impossible areas are gone.
Plot functions return the Figure and never call plt.show(); the starter's main block does that. In ax.hist, pass the non-missing values so the counts add up to the row count.
